Radial-velocity dataset seed29_diff3.

- 80 observations over a baseline of 55.1 days
- median reported uncertainty: 0.77 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 1 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 5

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Strong evidence for a 1-planet starting model.

Hypothesis:
- Planet b at 26.26 days

Why this period:
- The 26.26 d peak is overwhelmingly dominant (power 0.70, FAP ~ 0), far above all others.
- Its spectral-window power is low there, so it is not explained by cadence.
- The obvious relatives are 13.13 d and 52.51 d, but those are just half/double aliases of the same signal; 52.5 d is also close to the 55.1 d baseline, so the longer option is less well constrained.
- The other peaks near 0.9–1.1 d are classic daily-alias territory and not preferred over the strong 26.26 d signal.
- The 5.25 d peak is much weaker and only marginal by periodogram alone; per the “simplest model first” rule, it should be tested only after fitting the 26.26 d planet and inspecting residuals.

Please fit a 1-planet Keplerian/circular-start model at ~26.26 d, then check residuals for whether the 5.25 d signal survives significantly.
